title: Absence of supersymmetry at the LHC and the naturalness crisis
bottleneck: Supersymmetry was expected to appear near the weak scale to stabilize the Higgs mass against quantum corrections, but LHC Runs 1 through 3 have found no superpartners, pushing their masses into the multi-TeV range. The surviving parameter space requires the very fine-tuning supersymmetry was invented to avoid.
why_it_blocks: The hierarchy problem was the strongest phenomenological argument for new physics at colliders; its leading solution failing to materialize leaves the Standard Model's most puzzling feature unexplained and weakens the case for future colliders.
current_state: Attention has shifted to split supersymmetry, high-scale supersymmetry, and non-supersymmetric solutions like composite Higgs or extra dimensions, while the LHC continues searching in compressed and long-lived signatures. Split-supersymmetry and high-scale variants keep the mathematical structure while abandoning naturalness as a guiding principle.
